name: Cedar County, MO
findings: Cedar County has 53 nonprofit organizations. 20 of them (38%) list at least one way to get involved in their tax returns or on their websites: membership, volunteering, public events, or civic and political action.
The most common is membership, listed by 16 organizations.
Social and fraternal organizations are the largest group offering opportunities (50% of those with an identified type).
Compared with 10 similar places, Cedar County has about as many organizations offering opportunities per resident.
30% of the organizations offering opportunities have no identified type, so the breakdown by type is partial.

observations.title: Religious organizations that list no opportunities
observations.text: 6 religious organizations here list none of the four kinds of opportunity in their tax returns or on their websites. Many may still offer them without describing them there.

confidence.text: Based on 6 organizations here; 47% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: What do religious organizations here do in the community? How do people find out about them?

observations.title: More organizations list public events
observations.text: Per resident, more organizations in Cedar County list public events in their tax returns or on their websites than in 10 similar places (about 1.4 times the typical level).

confidence.text: Based on 13 organizations here; 47% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Why are public events so common here? Who takes part, and who might not be reached?

observations.title: Social and fraternal organizations stand out for membership
observations.text: 7 social and fraternal organizations here list membership, compared with about 2 in similar places of this size.

confidence.text: Based on 7 organizations here; 47% of all organizations here have no identified type.
